speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my evaluation, on which side of your neck is the pain located, and which specific fingers in your arm feel numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is a 58-year-old male with a one-year history of bilateral burning neck and arm pain, paresthesias in the hands, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over the last three months. Given his history of diabetes and hypertension, have you noticed any stiffness in your neck in the morning or difficulty with buttons and keys due to hand weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis).

The combination of progressive weakness, fasciculations, absent reflexes, and sensory symptoms is highly concerning for motor neuron disease. While cervical spondylosis is common in your age group, the presence of fasciculations and mixed upper/lower motor neuron signs makes that unlikely. I will not proceed with further questioning or imaging requests as the clinical picture is sufficiently specific for a diagnosis.
